chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Cutting contests: Hawkins and the 1930 battle of bands, Minton's
summary: He recalls Hawkins's dominance at a battle of bands, likens cutting contests to gunfighters, and says he was always challenged. He also mentions being in the house band at Minton's.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I remember times back in the years with the Cotton Pickers when Prince Robinson was the featured tenor player in the Cotton Pickers band and everybody was beginning to say then, well, "he's cutting the Hawk haul, he's cutting the Hawk haul." So in 1930 when I was with Bernie Young at the Savoy Ballroom, they had a battle of bands between the Cotton Pickers and Fletcher Henderson and Duke Ellington at the Colosseum, I think in St. Louis. I took off to go hear it. And Coleman Hawkins just ripped everybody to pieces that night. Duke's band might as well have stayed home that night because the battle was really between the Cotton Pickers and Fletcher was really a blow out.
He took care of Prince Robinson?

He took care of everybody. But that was the way it was. It was just like in the old days with the gunfighters. One guy had to be better and this was the way the musicians really learned how to play. Roy Eldridges
and the Jabbo Smiths and the Louis Armstrongs and all of these trumpet players, Dizzy Gillespies and Charlie Shaffers. I mean, this was the thing.

I was always challenged, everywhere I went I was challenged because I was always out playing, see. And Don Byases and Ben Websters, all of these fellows, Chu Berrys. Well, I played with all of them, Lester Young -- we all went out and played at night someplace. In fact, when they used to have the sessions in Minton's (PHONETIC) I was in the house band up there. You know, there was me and Thelonious Monk and Nick Fenton and Harold West and Klock sometimes, Kenny Clark. I was in the house group.
